utterances.speaker: ASIM KORICIC
utterances.text: I believe that they took care of that -- well, that is, at least, my information, but they took care of Sheheed families as we say, and I think that they took care of that, and how much they gave to who, that, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Let's talk about the uniforms of the 7th. They are identical to the uniforms worn by soldiers from other brigades of the army or was there a difference?

utterances.speaker: ASIM KORICIC
utterances.text: They were the same, like all others, but every brigade had its own symbol, its own insignia. The 7th Muslim Brigade had those saying "7th Muslim Brigade."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Therefore, individuals not belonging to the 7th Muslim Brigade, particularly the population, could they recognise members from the 7th from others or not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM KORICIC
utterances.text: A distinction could be made on the basis of the insignia. All the rest was the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Therefore, from your point of view, I can draw the conclusion that the only distinction was the insignia; did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: ASIM KORICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: What about the salary of the soldiers? Who paid them and how were they paid?

utterances.speaker: ASIM KORICIC
utterances.text: I personally received two salaries in the army. The first time, I think, was in June 1992. That is when these first Bosnian dinars came into being. This was a regular thing, and it went through the municipal staff. Later on, I did not receive anything, only -- I mean, if somebody would give me some kind of aid -- I did not receive a salary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: This situation of the salaries received and how they were received was the same for other brigades, or was there any difference for the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM KORICIC
utterances.text: At the time when I received a salary, it wasn't the 7th, and there was a regular list with one's name, rank, et cetera, and that made it possible to receive regular pay. I did not receive a salary in the 7th. Every now and then, for example, if I would travel, I didn't have any money, and then once or twice I addressed the Islamic Centre so that they would give me some assistance, if they could help me out, because we had no money flow. I personally did not have any money.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: This would be my last question. It relates to the relationship between the 7th and General Hadzihasanovic and/or the staff, the general staff. What was this relationship, particularly within the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: ASIM KORICIC
utterances.text: The system was just as my subordinate units had to act in accordance with the code of conduct, the regulations, there is reporting. There are team meetings of every commander and various questions are looked into, and then the commander gives an order or certain instructions, so this is done in the spirit of the regulations, that is to say, certain decisions are passed and they are binding. So there is this vertical line of decision-making, of command, and there is a horizontal line, and those are the logistics and other units that do not have the power to decide on certain other matters like the command does. So if an order comes, it is my duty to carry it out or, rather, to send it out lower and lower and lower to that level that is responsible for a certain task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: And these orders, you received them from the staff or from General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM KORICIC
utterances.text: If the order comes from the general staff, then the command of the corps says as follows: "On the basis of the order issued by the general staff, I issue the following order, which is binding," or we say, "Please act in accordance with," et cetera, et cetera. That's what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Koricic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Judge Rodrigues. I don't have any particular questions. I asked a lot at the beginning of your testimony. Thank you very much. And through you, we thank your government, which cooperated with the International Criminal Tribunal. You may be released. The usher will help you, and we will ask the next witness to come before this court. Thank you very much, Mr. Koricic. (The witness withdrew) (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can you hear me? Can you hear me, Colonel or Mr. Kubura? Look at the President. Can you hear me? Can you hear me in your language? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can hear you and I understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. We would like to know your name, surname, place and date of birth, and current occupation. After that, you will read the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Amir Kubura, born on the 4th of March, 1964, in Kakanj, Bosnia-Herzegovina. At present, I am in the command of the 1st Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What is your rank, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Colonel. Very well. We will call you Colonel then. Please be seated, but after you've read the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. You can now be seated. Thank you, Colonel, for coming here on the request of the Trial Chamber who wanted to hear your testimony because it seems that you were a significant player in all the events which led to this trial, the Prosecutor against the accused, for criminal acts that he allegedly committed. The accused is here on your left-hand side. After two years of trial, we wished to have clarification on your functions of commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade. You read the documents that were sent to you by the Chamber, and we decided that the theme of your testimony would be the organisation -- well, first of all, the role and the function that you had at the relevant dates, then the organisation and the structure of the command of the 7th Muslim Brigade of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the 7th Muslim Brigade, as it was called. You also know that we want your opinion and your point of view on the deployment on the ground of this brigade and its range of action, and then we asked you the perception you had of the conflict between the Croats and the Muslims in Central Bosnia between August 1993 and January 1994, at least during the period when you were commander of this brigade. On that point, we would like to know what information you received and what happened in Dusina. We would like to know what information you have on the treatment of prisoners that we heard during this trial on different sides, and then what was your impression of the accused, if you have one. These are the main themes of your testimony. We are now ready to hear you. You can express yourself freely. I hope you didn't prepare your testimony in advance, although you can use personal notes to refresh your memory. After this, the Prosecution and the Defence will ask you a certain number of questions, if they wish to do so, and the Judges may also have some questions for you, and we will stop at 1.00. I think that half an hour will be enough for you to testify. Otherwise, you will have more time after the break. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. First, I would like to deal with the first question that was put to me, and that is the organisation or structure of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: First of all, I'm sorry to interrupt from the very beginning, I'll try not to do this, but we would like to know, given the witness we have heard before, we would like to know what were the dates you were commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade, from which date to which date you were commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade; and then after that, you will be able to proceed on the organisation and the structure of the command of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before I begin, I would like to remind you of the following: That before I came here, two days before I came here, I received a list of questions that I was supposed to answer here, that is to say, that I had a very short period of time to prepare myself; and in view of this very short notice, I managed to prepare myself to the best of my ability, so perhaps I won't be able to mention all the dates, but I shall give you the tentative dates and I shall let you know about this. Through these remarks that I shall be making, through these questions, I am going to give you these intervals and the time and the dates. The organisation and structure of the command of the 7th Muslim Brigade within the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Sorry, Colonel. I'm sorry, but either you know when you started occupying this position as commander or you don't know. When were you appointed? When did you become commander? It seems to me it is a very simple question, or else you can answer that you don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely. In December 1992, on the basis of the order issued by the command of the 3rd Corps, I was sent to the 7th Muslim Brigade in the 3rd Corps. Until then, I was commander of the battalion in Kakanj. I was transferred and I was appointed the assistant chief of staff for operative and teaching affairs. In 1993, I was appointed chief of staff of the brigade, and I was appointed commander of the brigade by an order issued in August 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is to say, that the brigade was established in November on the basis of an order issued by the supreme command. The brigade was of an operative tactical nature. Within its composition, it had a command, units attached to the staff, and, at the very beginning, it had two battalions. When I say "the very beginning," I'm referring to November and December. And in January, the 3rd Battalion was established. The average number of men in the brigade during the war when I was in the brigade was between 1500 and 1800 men. The brigade was armed with infantry arms, and about 60 per cent of all the requirements of the brigade were met. The brigade had two specific characteristics, and they were the following: The first one was that it was extraterritorial in the sense that the men came from several different municipalities, and the second specific characteristic was that the brigade has full freedom of practising religion. When I mention this first specific characteristic, I wish to say the following, that the units got their men from Zenica, Kakanj, Travnik, Busovaca, Vitez, that is to say, the municipalities where the brigade was deployed. When I spoke of this other specific characteristic and when I said freedom of practising religion, I wish to say that, within the brigade, there were certain premises called mesdzid for performing religious rites and also there were a certain number of persons called imams. These were religious officials who performed religious services. I wish to point out that in respect of these specific characteristics, within the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there were other such brigades too. There were three brigades of this nature, in the second brigade -- two in the 1st Corps and one in the 4th Corps. Throughout its existence, the brigade was within the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It received all its orders from the commander of the 3rd Corps. In the brigade, there was subordination from the brigade vis-à-vis the corps and within the brigade between the battalions and the units attached to the staff. I have already pointed out when I was transferred to the brigade. When I arrived in the brigade, when I came to the brigade, Asim Koricic was commander of the brigade. That is what I would like to say in respect of the first question. Now I would like to move on to the second question, and it had to do with the deployment of the brigade on the ground, as well as its area of operation. The brigade was deployed on the ground as follows with regard to command posts: The command and the staff units were in Zenica; the 2nd Battalion was also in Zenica, the 1st Battalion in Travnik, the 3rd Battalion in Kakanj, but one company of the 3rd Battalion was in Kacuni, the municipality of Busovaca. As regards the engagement and area of activity of the brigade, I would like to speak about everything I came to know, starting from December 1992 throughout my stay there, that is to say, until April 1994. In December 1992, on the basis of an order issued by the command of the corps, the brigade was redeployed to the front at Visoko where it was resubordinated to the Istok Operative Group with its headquarters in Visoko. The task of the brigade was to carry out defence operations vis-à-vis the army of Republika Srpska, bearing in mind the situation that was taking place in Sarajevo, that is to say, to disburden our forces in Sarajevo. As for the Visoko front line, at the end of December, within combat operations, the brigade suffered great losses in manpower; almost 40 soldiers were killed and 60 were gravely wounded or lightly wounded. After that task in January, the brigade returned to Zenica, according to the orders issued by the corps command, in order to consolidate, to train, and prepare for further use. Bearing in mind the mentioned losses, the brigade, during the months of January and February, did not receive any major assignments. In January, its zone of responsibility was at Bijelo Bucje, that is, above Travnik, vis-à-vis the army of Republika Srpska. The focus within that zone of responsibility centred around the 1st Battalion of our brigade, although within that zone, there were other battalions that were engaged there in order to alleviate the burden on the manpower. Also, in January, one company was attached to the municipal staff of defence of Zenica in order to help them within their own zone of responsibility in terms of organisation. Now the month of February. In February, the brigade was redeployed at the Visoko front line and stayed in the village of Ramadanovci and Luke. The brigade was redeployed in February, that is to say, two-thirds of the 2nd Battalion and one-third of the 1st Battalion. The rest of the brigade, in February, was carrying out preparations for redeployment. At the beginning of March, the entire brigade was redeployed at the Visoko front line. In the month of March, the situation was very difficult once again. In Sarajevo, our forces were having a difficult time, so our task was, in the month of March, to tie up the forces of the army of Republika Srpska to the Visoko front line so that things would be easier for our units in Sarajevo because the situation in Sarajevo was difficult, that is to say, that the brigade was at the Visoko front line in March, and then after that, the beginning of April, the brigade returned from the Visoko front line to Zenica to get some rest and to prepare for future use. At that time, in Zenica, there was a deterioration of relations between HVO units and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The HVO took Zmajevac Kuber, Saracevica and, as you say, certain facilities, also parts of town, and Cajdras and other parts of town, so the situation was deteriorating between HVO units and the army. In those days, in the spirit of the orders issued by the command of the 3rd Corps, these areas that were taken over, these parts of Zenica that were taken over were liberated, and also the road that then led from Zenica to Travnik, that was also jeopardised at the time. The part of the Busovaca front line towards Kula, above the village of Visnjica, was jeopardised then. At that time, in the spirit of the orders issued by the command of the 3rd Corps, the 2nd Battalion was issued orders with regard to Kula. June. In the month of June, HVO units cut off the road between Zenica and Travnik. Relations were strained because of that in the territory of Ovnak between the HVO units and the units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In the spirit of the orders issued by the command of the 3rd Corps, the brigade was, together with the other brigades then and the municipal staff and also the police unit of the Ministry of Defence, it was engaged in liberating parts of the Zenica-Travnik road. Most probably in order to disburden that zone, the HVO units in Kakanj at the time took over important facilities around Kakanj and also parts of the town itself. At that point in time, the corps command ordered the liberation of parts of Kakanj and of those facilities, and within that assignment, in addition to the units and the brigades that were involved in this task, my brigade came to carry out this task too. After this task, the brigade returned to Zenica. In July, the situation was aggravated between the HVO units and the Armija of the Kiseljak and Busovaca theatres, where, in the estimate of the 3rd Corps command, most probably an attempt was being made to link Kiseljak and Busovaca so that Fojnica could be separated from Visoko. On the basis of the orders of the corps command, I redeployed my unit to Bilalovac, in order to carry out defence operations and to prevent HVO units from carrying out their own assignment. At that time, that is to say, in the month of June, the situation in the Igman plateaux worsened where the units of the army of Republika Srpska were launching an offensive towards Bijelasnica and Igman. The army lost large parts of its territory at the time, and then I received orders to send a part of the 1st Battalion to the Igman plateaux, and that is what I did in order to help our units. August. In the month of August, the brigade returned from the Kiseljak-Fojnica front line to Zenica. The unit from Igman returned to Zenica, and in August, the zone that I had in Bijelo Bucje, above Travnik, I handed over in the spirit of the order issued by the command of the corps to the Operative Group Bosanska Krajina. At that time, again relations were strained between the HVO units and the army in Vitez. The situation was difficult. Part of a unit of ours that was in Stari Vitez at the time was in a particularly difficult situation. In the spirit of the order of the command of the 3rd Corps, I redeployed the brigade to the Vitez theatre, and I then attached them to the Operative Group of Bosanska Krajina. In the spirit of this command, I put the brigade in Sadovace, Bukve and Poculica. My task at the time was, within this zone of defence, to carry out defensive combat activities in order to disburden our units that were in Stari Vitez at the time. At that time, the brigade stayed in that zone until October. In October, it returned to Zenica to get some rest. At that time --

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: At that time, relations became strained between the BH army and the HVO units in Vares.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the English?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I can hear the French booth.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the English booth?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Start again, please, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. So at that time, as I said, relations became strained between the HVO units and the BH army in Vares, and the HVO blocked the road from Vares to Olovo, which was the only alternative road, that is to say, the only road going towards Tuzla. The commander of the Operative Group from Visoko was taken into custody, and, according to certain information, he was transferred via Serbian territory into Kiseljak. Within the straining of relations and in the spirit of the order issued by the 3rd Corps command, my command was relocated and gained assignments at the Vares battleground and joined the Operative Group of Vares in this theatre, which was within the composition of the 6th Corps. Within the frameworks of this blockade on that road, the 6th, 3rd, and 2nd Corps took part, and my brigade was within the composition of the rest of the units. According to the assignment and according to our assessment, probably part of the units of the HVO were transferred from the Vares battlefront via the territory which was under the control of the army of the Republika Srpska into Kiseljak. In November, that is to say, the HVO units, in November, launched an attack from Kiseljak towards Fojnica, and in this connection, they took control of part of the territory of Jaskovica, Citonja, and part of Fojnica. Obojak, that is part of Fojnica. Because the situation was very difficult in Fojnica, the population left Fojnica, fled from Fojnica. On the basis of an order from my command, I was assigned to relocate the group to Fojnica, and it was my assignment to win back the territory that had been lost in order to stabilise life in Fojnica and for the people to be able to return, and this I did with the other units in that zone. After that assignment, the situation was difficult in Kacuni, which is the zone under the control of the BH army and facing Busovaca. In view of the fact that I was in the vicinity, I was in Fojnica, I was assigned the task of relocating the brigade and deploying it in Kacuni and Zioci (phoen). Those are villages near Busovaca. The task was, from that side, the Busovaca side, to ensure security for the zone and to prevent loss of territory. Once I had completed my assignment, I returned the brigade to Zenica in the spirit of the command I received, that is to say, in January, I took the brigade back to Zenica in January. In the spirit of the order from the command of the 3rd Corps, my 1st Battalion, which until then had been attached to the operative group of Bosanska Krajina, was decommanded into the operative group of Bosanska Krajina, it was separated from it, and I received orders to establish the 1st Battalion, which is what I, in fact, did. In the course of the month of February, we focused on training, reorganisation, and the establishment of that battalion. At the beginning, that is to say, at the end of February and the beginning of March, relations became strained in Zavidovici and the battleground there, and the municipality of Maglaj found itself in a difficult situation because it was under attack by the army of the Republika Srpska, and in order to help the Maglaj municipality, and once again within the spirit of the order of the 3rd Corps command, I relocated the brigade to Zavidovici and the assignment was the following: to defend the area and to tie up, engage, the army of the Republika Srpska towards Zavidovici in order to unburden the municipality of Maglaj. In March, I was in Zavidovici with the brigade, and I returned in April. After that, that is to say, at the beginning of April, I received an order from the supreme command, and I was moved from the 3rd to the 4th Corps. As regards the second question, that was the chronology I had. Now I go on to the third subject matter, the Croatian-Muslim conflict between August '93 to the end of January '94 and its consequences. I have already stressed that in August, the brigade was at the Kiseljak-Fojnica theatre of operations, and in August it returned from the Kiseljak-Fojnica theatre to Zenica. In August, I already stressed that I gave over the zone of responsibility of Bijelo Bucje to the operative group of Bosanska Krajina. The situation in September was difficult in relation to Vitez --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I don't want you to go through the chronology again. We've heard it once already. On behalf of my colleagues and myself, I would like to hear your testimony about important events, such as the kidnapping of Commander Totic or events which may have taken place in Dusina and about the problem of detainees, if there were any, and their treatment. Could you please help us on these very precise points since you gave us in a very detailed manner all your activities as a commander, military commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. I touched upon this entire area in answer to the second question, so I don't wish to repeat that. As far as the questions that you raised are concerned ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber would like you to focus on crucial points of which we have heard for two years. I'm sure you were a very professional and conscientious military chief, but we are more interested in a certain number of events which took place during the conflict, how you perceived the cease-fire, what were the activities of the 7th Brigade and, of course, the Prosecution and the Defence will ask you further questions, also the Judges will do that. But please focus on the very important points I have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You first asked me something in connection with Zivko Totic. As far as that is concerned, I have no information about that nor do I personally know Zivko Totic nor did I know which assignment he was carrying out or which post he held. As far as Dusina is concerned, I would be interested in knowing the period of time you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I do note that you don't know exactly if there were crimes committed in Dusina. Therefore, we will ask for questions from the parties and from the Judges. But through your question, I can draw the conclusion that you don't know if there were particular events which took place in Dusina. Can I draw that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From what I said a moment ago, the engagement of my units, we could see where my brigade was engaged, and that is the complete zone where the brigade was present; and with respect to Dusina and the war crime that you have mentioned, I know nothing about that and can tell you nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. I take note of your answer. You know nothing about that. You were holding your position at the time, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I held a position, yes. From December until February, I was the deputy assistant of the chief of staff of the brigade and then became the chief of staff of the brigade and commander of the brigade in August, August 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I see. Please proceed with your testimony and we will ask you some questions. Proceed with your testimony, if you have anything to add, but don't give us a very detailed military chronology. You were not summoned here to tell us about all the events which happened from a military point of view. We are absolutely convinced that a lot of things happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as that period of time is concerned, bearing in mind that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time engaged in a lot of fighting with the units of the army of Republika Srpska, at that time we did not want a second front to be open towards the HVO units, and the corps command at that time signed a number of agreements between the Armija and the HVO units. There were some zones where we held the line together facing the Serbian army. However, at that time the HVO units froze their relations with the units of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We have a lot of information on this aspect, Colonel. We heard a lot of military experts. That was not the point of our question. Let's now go to the last theme of your testimony: Did you have a direct or indirect impression of the role of the accused, "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never had any direct contacts. I am seeing him for the first time. In the course of the war, everything that was signed, I consider that he should have done his all for -- everything signed to be implemented, but that was not the case. Personally, I cannot say anything because I don't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Of course not. Do you have anything to add before the break, before the lunch break? You will be coming back after, at 2.30. Do you have any other important elements to add?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said what I wanted in my introduction, and that would be all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Mr. Prosecutor, will you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will have no questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Nobilo, will you have any questions for this witness at 2.30?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. President, I will have some questions to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thirty minutes, just like before?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. We will now take the lunch break, and we will resume our work at 2.30. Thank you. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Have the accused brought in. We will resume work. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, you have the floor for about half an hour for your questions to the witness of the Court. After that, I shall ask my colleagues if they have any questions they wish to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I shall try to speed things up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Colonel, good afternoon. My colleague, Russell Hayman and myself, Anto Nobilo, represent General Blaskic. On behalf of the Defence, I have a couple of questions for you. Would you tell me first, please, who was the commander from March 1993 to August 1993? Actually, this morning, we heard Colonel Koricic, who said that you had been the commander of the 7th Muslim from July 1993 until August 1993 -- from March 1993 until August 1993, that you had been the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Who is right?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: Mr. President, this period, from March 1993 to August 1993, during that period, the commander of the brigade, Asim Koricic, was absent from the country in line with the approval he had received from the command of the 3rd Corps. As the chief of staff at the time, I represented the commander, and in August, I was actually appointed commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Colonel Koricic told us that he was in Zagreb. On what business was he there?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: Colonel Koricic addressed the request to the corps command, and it was granted for him to be absent for that period of time; however, he had not intended to stay all that long. In view of the relations at the time, in order to reach Zenica from Croatia, because of personal security reasons, he couldn't come back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You're not answering the question. I think the question was what took Colonel Koricic to Zagreb? You can answer or not. It is up to you.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, his family was abroad. I think that was the cause.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were there any so-called Mujahedins in the 7th Muslim Brigade, foreigners, mostly from Arab countries?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: Throughout my service in the 7th Muslim, from November until April 1994, there were no foreigners, nor did they figure in the records, which can be confirmed from those lists and reports to the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about the El Mujahed detachment? Did it have a special relationship with the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: Until April of 1994, I was in the 7th Muslim Brigade, and up until then, the El Mujahed detachment did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us now view a short video of three or four seconds. It is a clip, a short clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. Nobilo, it is up to you. You have every liberty to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us dim the lights, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That will suffice as an introduction to a question. Was this the typical appearance of the Mujahedin, who appeared within the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps, visually?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I have already said that while I was in office, the El Mujahed did not exist, nor do I recognise any one of these fighters. So people like this were not members of my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But did such soldiers appear within the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: But I was not the commander of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But you moved around within the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. Did you ever see soldiers who looked like this coming from Arab countries in the course of 1993 in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: Where I was with my brigade, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When the kidnapped Zivko Totic was exchanged for captured Mujahedins held in the Kaonik prison, were you in Zenica at the time?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: What period was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Sometime in May '93.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: At that time, I was the brigade commander. Regarding the captured Zivko Totic, I do not know anything about it, nor can I provide any answer. I didn't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But were you present when they were exchanged? This was a spectacular event in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: No, because it was the corps command that was in charge of that operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But were you present or were you not present? You are not answering the questions put to you.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I was not present, and I never saw Zivko Totic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us go on to the wartime activities of your brigade. According to the testimony of Asim Koricic, the brigade commander at the time, we're talking about January 1993, a battalion of the 7th Muslim, under the command of Serif Patkovic, carried out an operation in Dusina. At the time you were head of operations in the brigade, will you tell us, please, who gave orders to Serif Patkovic to attack Dusina or, rather, his battalion?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: No one gave him such orders, nor did Serif Patkovic go to Dusina. I said earlier on that that month, on the basis of an order from a superior command, a company was attached to the municipal staff. That company was under the jurisdiction of the municipal staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In January '93, from the 25th of January, 1993 onwards, the area from Kacuni to Bilalovac, you said -- who ordered that unit to go to Dusina? Who was the person who issued the order to advance on Dusina?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: That unit, in accordance with an order of the corps command, was attached to the municipal staff. It was a unit that was the strength of a company. The commander of that company was the late Fahrudin Camdzic who was killed in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But who gave orders to that company to advance on Dusina?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I said that it was subordinated to the municipal staff of Zenica. The command of the municipal staff was in command of that company.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know the commander of the municipal staff of Zenica at the time?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: At that time, it was Colonel Jasmin Saric.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that the 7th Muslim Brigade, in January and February, was in the area of Kacuni and Bilalovac. I should like documents D444, D445, and D446 to be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I don't know whether that's an error in the transcript. I heard "454, 455, and 456." Which are the exact numbers, please, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I asked for Defence Exhibits D444, D445 and D446.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: While the document is being prepared, let me ask, did any information reach you and do you know anything about the fact that between Kacuni and Bilalovac, Croatian villages were plundered and burned, so that a total of 423 houses were destroyed in the villages of Bukovci, Grablje, Gusti Grab, Javor, Jelinak, Kacuni, Krvavicici, Kula, Milavici, Nezirovici, Poseliste, Prosje, Putis, Solakovici, and Turici. At the time that your unit was in this area, are you familiar with any of this?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: You didn't understand that correctly. In February, the unit went to the villages of Luke, Ramadanovci in Visoko municipality, in that part of the Kiseljak-Busovaca theatre of operations. So it had no assignment in relation to HVO units but, rather, it was confronted with units of Republika Srpska; and what you are saying about these villages and burnt houses, I know nothing about that nor were my units engaged there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you claim that the 7th Muslim, in January and February, was not in this area that I have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: It was not in that whole area that you have listed nor did it have any assignments in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But were you near Kacuni?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: We were in Kacuni later on, as I said in my previous chronology. That was later on, not in the month that you have referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In that case, we withdraw these exhibits because these are photos of burnt houses and, as the witness says that his unit was not there at the time, we will withdraw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: However, your unit, in April, was withdrawn to Zenica. When did it start to engage in combat, on what date; could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: At that time, that is, in April, it was deployed following orders from the corps command. It was used in the territory of Zenica municipality. I have the month April noted, but not the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, do you know the villages of Grm, Cajdras, Podbrezje near Zenica?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I know the village of Cajdras as it is rather large.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was the 7th Muslim active in that area?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: Not in the area of Cajdras but only in the area of Zenica and Zmajevac. Not in Cajdras.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Cajdras, Grm, Podbrezje, it did not act there? Could the witness be shown Exhibit D451? This is Defence Exhibit D451, and it represents a statement of the mother of a little girl who was killed, Ivanka Zrnic, and the father of the girl who was killed, Zeljko Zrnic. I will read a part of it. The event occurred in Cajdras. I am reading from it. After the word "Statement," the text begins: (as read) "On the 18th of April, 1993, I (Ivanka Zrnic) was in the house with my family. I was awakened by loud shooting, and we all took shelter on the ground floor of the house, of the same house at my mother-in-law's. There was my husband, two children, mother-in-law, uncle, aunt, cousin, his wife, and three little girls. I later found out that only eleven of us stayed behind while all the others had fled from Cajdras, and nobody informed us what was going on. In addition to us, two elderly persons from our neighbourhood stayed behind and were later killed: They were Ivan Vidovic, born in 1904, and Anto Vidovic, born in 1906. Ivan was taken out and shot and then his house was set on fire. Anto was killed in the house. We were lying on the floor when a Muslim soldier from the 7th Muslim Brigade approached the window and, without a word, fired a whole clip of an automatic rifle at us. On this occasion, my daughter Magdalena, three and a half years old, was hit, and she died almost instantly. She was hit in the right cheek, and the exit wound was at the back of her head. I too was wounded in the head." The text continues with a description of the event, and the parents ended up in the music school and they described how they were treated in that music school. Colonel, do you know anything about this event and similar events in Croatian villages around Zenica?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I know nothing about this event. The village of Cajdras was not in that area. What is more, in the village of Cajdras, there was no fighting in view of the fact that members of HVO units in Cajdras had requested a police unit to surrender their weapons. More detailed information can be provided by representatives of the MUP in Zenica. I think more than 300 barrels were surrendered. My brigade was not engaged in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How do you explain the fact that this witness saw a soldier from the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I don't see how she could have recognised which unit that soldier belonged to. I repeat, my unit was not engaged there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But didn't members of your brigade carry insignia on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: She couldn't have recognised any of my soldiers because they weren't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were your soldiers in the village of Miletici when a large number of civilians were killed in the village of Miletici? Where is the village of Miletici?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I don't know. I was not there on assignment because, otherwise, I would know the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that in June you were assigned to carry out a combat operation at Ovnak, and in doing so, you linked Travnik with Zenica. Let me read to you some figures, and could Exhibit D528 be prepared? At that time, in June 1993, in the village of Dolac, the following civilians were killed in their homes: Ankica Bursic, Tomo Bilecic, Milka Blazevic, Ivo Marijanovic, a woman called Luca who was staying in an old people's home, Josip Medic, Juro Herceg, Viktor Svalina, Finka Bojanovic, Finka Perndes, Cedo Prosina. All were killed in their homes in the village of Dolac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Nobilo. Are you reading from an exhibit, and if so, could you give me the exhibit number so I can find it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am not reading from an exhibit, I am reading my own prepared questions and my own notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, Colonel, are you familiar with this event?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: You asked me regarding the unit on assignment there. In my previous statement, I said that the brigade, together with other brigades, the municipal staff, and a unit of the MUP police was engaged on assignment to lift the blockade on the Zenica-Travnik road, and within the framework of that assignment, the brigade was active. I am not familiar with the data you have just read out. I think that that information is not linked to my unit. It is the first time I come across that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the same day, the village of Ovnak, that is, on the 8th of June, 1993, in that village several Croatian houses were set on fire. A man called Cuturic, born in 1917, was killed; in the neighbouring village, another four civilians were killed; in Dolac Bila, two civilians; and on the same day, in the village of Cukle, also a neighbouring village to Ovnak, 19 Croatian civilians; and in Brajkovici, seven Croatian civilians. All this on the 8th of June, 1993, in the area in which your brigade was stationed. Do you know anything about any of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me. Again, Mr. Nobilo, Your Honours, my request is to know if this is an exhibit that is in evidence or if this is Mr. Nobilo's personal notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, objection sustained. You must specify, Mr. Nobilo, whether this is from an exhibit. If so, you must cite which exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I already said, these are the same notes that I am using for my questions. However, numerous exhibits are already in evidence, but in the interest of efficiency, I opted not to show them to the witness. I just wanted to have this reminder in front of me to be able to ask my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. In your written notes, obviously, you will specify the point if you intend to elaborate on it so that the Prosecution may respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me repeat in summary form. My question is: On the 8th of June, 1993, in the village of Ovnak and the surrounding villages, Grahovcici, Dolac Bila, Cukle, Dolac, Postinje, Podovi, a large number of civilians were killed and a large number of houses burned. Let us forget the names. Do you know anything at all about those events? Was this done by soldiers from the 7th Muslim Brigade? Did you see the houses burning? Did you see dead civilians?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: The villages that you have mentioned, some of them I am familiar with, and all of them are between Ovnak and Travnik. My assignment was between Zenica and Ovnak, so some of the villages that you have mentioned and which I am familiar with were not within my area, the area of my assignment. But you also don't have the right date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Refresh my memory, please. You were the head of the 7th Muslim Brigade at that time --

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: It was the 9th of June. As far as I remember, it was the 9th of June, not the 8th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No, I am asking you whether you were indeed commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade at that time.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: Yes, I was at the head of the 7th Muslim Brigade, but I am saying that these activities did not occur on the 8th but on the 9th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. But they took place, and those villages were indeed burned. This did happen.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: No, I said that the villages listed, some of them I know. They are between Ovnak and Travnik. My assignment had to do up to Ovnak with my brigade. What happened in the rear, behind, towards Travnik, I can't say because I'm not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Continue, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us accept that it was on the 9th. But tell us then, which villages were included by your operations from Zenica to Ovnak; could you tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: From Zenica to Ovnak, there were no villages. It was Ovnak, in fact. And when we say Ovnak, I'm not speaking about the village of Ovnak but the region of Ovnak. It's a hill which is called Ovnak. It's a hill, and this is the communication line from Zenica to Travnik. It runs across that line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the village of Ovnak was burnt?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: This part, in the zone where my unit was, it was not burnt, and among other things, it is common knowledge that in that particular zone, there is a monastery, and the monastery was secured by platoon, a unit was there to secure it, and nobody touched it. That is common knowledge. So there was no burning, and the monastery stands today and is used today, so it was not ablaze, nor was it destroyed; it was secured. The people that were in the warehouse were taken to a safe zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But tell the Trial Chamber, please, whether you entered the village of Ovnak or not, your brigade.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: So you're speaking about the village of Ovnak, and I am speaking about the communication road in my area. That's the difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that your responsibility was from Zenica to Ovnak, and I'm asking you whether your units entered the village of Ovnak or not.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: So I came to the village of Ovnak with my unit on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you enter the village?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: From the village of Ovnak, the people with HVO units, that is to say, the HVO units withdrew the people towards Vitez at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you enter the village of Ovnak? I'm asking you this for the third time.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: And after that, the village of Ovnak was empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you enter the village of Ovnak? I'm asking you that for the fourth time.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: After that time, when the village was empty, the units which were in that zone, that is to say, that the several brigades, the municipal staff and the military police, and with the police of the corps, they entered the village, in the aim of protecting the village and preventing any irregular acts from taking part and in order to protect the monastery. That was the command of the corps. It was our aim to protect.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you did not enter the village of Ovnak with your unit; can we conclude that?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: Let me repeat, into the village of Ovnak, the units which were on assignment there sent their units of the military police, and the corps police unit entered to secure the zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The question is did you enter the village, "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well then. Just give us your answer, please. If we wish to proceed quickly, please answer the question. Let me remind you of the text that you should be familiar with. First of all, it is a text that protects you. I'm going to read it to you. "A witness may refuse to make any statement which could incriminate him. The Chamber, nevertheless, can force the witness to answer. Of course, no testimony obtained in this way can be used subsequently as evidence against the witness, except in case of perjury." So you are not risking anything. You are not risking anything before these Judges. You cannot refuse to answer. Only in a case of perjury can you be called to task. When a question is put to you, you have to answer it. We can't accept the same question being put to you four times. Did you or did you not enter the village?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Apart from Ovnak, did you, in the period to come, enter into the Travnik municipality, and were your units in the area of the municipality of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer. The interpreter did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Would you repeat the answer, please? We went too fast and the interpreters weren't able to hear your answer. So the question was: Did the 7th Muslim Brigade spend any time in the municipality of Travnik from June 1993 onwards?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: The brigade, as a brigade, was not in the Travnik municipality. It was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And parts of the 7th Muslim Brigade, were they not located in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: In Travnik, as I said first, where our first battalion was located, and he had an area of responsibility towards Bijelo Bucje, facing the army of the Republika Srpska, but not Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But, Colonel, if your battalion was in Travnik, then the 7th Muslim Brigade was in Travnik as well, because was not that battalion part of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I've already said that it was part of the 7th Muslim Brigade and that the battalion had this line of responsibility towards the army of the Republika Srpska, and it was contrary to the area that you are talking about, so the brigade was not in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I asked about the municipality of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Isn't it a battalion of --

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: Bijelo Bucje, yes, that's where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you, in the course of your work, as the chief of staff and deputy chief of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and it spent some time in the Travnik municipality, did you receive the following information, that is to say, that in the municipality of Travnik, 1.450 Croatian houses had been burnt and that 40 to 60 per cent of them had been destroyed, and I'm reading from D528, and that Croatian houses were destroyed between 20 to 40 per cent, 1.080, and devastated, 840, et cetera. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I am hearing this data for the first time here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you hear that in the Travnik municipality, there was destruction to numerous churches, such as, for example, Bukovica in the Guca Gora parish, Dolac in the Dolac parish, Gornji Dolac, in the Dolac parish, and it is the cemetery, one of the oldest cemetery in the region. Did you hear about the fact that in the municipality of Travnik, these sacral buildings were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: These are, once again, my notes and not part of a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Just a point of clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I will remind you, Mr. Nobilo, that this is a Court witness, and at some point, either in your brief or at any other point, you will give us references to these notes, but it is quite normal that the Prosecutor knows in what stage of the proceedings you obtained these figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: From your battalion, the 7th Muslim Brigade, did you receive any information that a series of Catholic churches and places of worship were destroyed in the municipality of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: No, I did not receive information of that kind. I was not informed of that. Let me mention that my brigade, in the municipality of Travnik, never fought against the HVO units. The only assignment that it had was the assignment of the 1st Battalion at Bijelo Bucje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But you did engage in combat activities in Kakanj. You said you had liberated Kakanj. Do you know that 15.000 Croats fled Kakanj? Do you know that piece of data?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: No, I don't know that figure. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But when you liberated Kakanj and the villages of the Kakanj municipality, did you encounter empty villages and destroyed houses?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: During my assignment in Kakanj, in addition to my brigade and following the command, there were other units taking part. The HVO units, with part of the population, not all the population, but part of the population, did move out of Kakanj and Kraljevska Sutjeska to Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you see Croatian villages ablaze?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us carry on with the war paths of your brigade. You said that in August you came to Vitez at the Sadovace, Bukve, and Poculica villages, that you arrived there. Do you know anything about the following, that is to say, that at that time, in that area, in your zone of responsibility, 17 civilians were captured belonging to a work platoon, Croats who were there cutting down the forests, taking wood for firewood, for timber, and that they were captured and killed? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: In August, the brigade was at the Vitez battleground, but what you have just said I have heard for the first time. I did not know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: May I have D440, please, document D440?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Remind the Court when you came to the Vares municipality with your unit, please.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: At the beginning of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We are now going to show a video clip which was taken in Vares precisely at the time when your unit was there. It is Defence Exhibit D531. Would you look at all the soldiers carefully, please? Perhaps you'll recognise some of them. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is the Croatian village of Pogar. Do you recognise these scenes, this truck, these people?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I recognise neither the scene, nor the people, nor the trucks. I don't know the location of the village of Pogar. Had it been in my zone, I would have remembered the locality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was there any looting, killing, and mass burning of houses in Vares at the time when you were there with your unit?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: The unit was engaged with the other units of the 6th Corps, the 2nd Corps, and the 3rd Corps, and as far as I know, there was none of this in Vares, and Vares remained a town that had not been set ablaze.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But I'm asking you about the villages in the Vares municipality?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: In the zone under my command, as far as I know, this did not exist. In the other zones, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you define your area of responsibility for us in precise terms, please? In Vares, your zone of responsibility in Vares, please.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: With my unit, I entered Vares along the road. I took the road into Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before you entered Vares, did you pass by any villages?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: The road I took, I saw no burned houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is D440, it's a large Defence Exhibit, and it describes everything that refers to the village of Vares, and we can stop the tape now. Let us move forward. Your next stop along your path in Central Bosnia was Fojnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could I have Defence Exhibit D153 now, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: While we're preparing the document, D153, I should like to ask you whether you are conscious of the fact that 6.000 Croats were expelled from Fojnica at the time when your unit entered Fojnica.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I am not aware of that, nor do I know anything about that piece of information because at that time, the Bosniak people had left Fojnica and were moving towards Visoko because part of Fojnica had already fallen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Are you testifying that the Croats were not expelled from Fojnica but that it was the Bosniaks who were expelled?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I had not been informed about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We're now going to read a document to you. It is in English. I don't know how far you understand English. My colleague will read the document out. It is document, Defence Exhibit, D153.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If the third page of this document could be put on the ELMO, that would assist the interpreters, I think, and I'll be reading from this ECMM background report, titled "Fojnica," the date on it is termed "last update 6 October 1993," and the paragraph I would like to read is on page 3, it's titled "Ethnic Minorities." It's in the bottom half of the page. The paragraph states -- and there are some words on the left-hand margin, Mr. President, that are not legible. I'll do the best I can. "Fojnica has a Catholic monastery where are living 17 religious people. The remaining Croats come here to find any kind of help." Then it appears: "From the former 6500 Croats, only 100/150 remain, and the last info (unintelligible) from the guardian of the monastery indicate an hostile (unintelligible) from the Muslim majority. The houses which were previously occupied by Croats have been first looted, then burnt and destroyed, all along the period of July/August and September. We have observed this slow evolution, particularly on the road south of Fojnica in Drin and Bakovici."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Colonel, you made the statement that you made, and now I would like to ask you: How do you explain the fact that wherever the 7th Muslim Brigade turned up, the Croats were expelled, the houses, hundreds and thousands of Croatian houses, were burnt and looted; is that a coincidence or something else? How do you explain this?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: You mention July, August, and September. At that time, I stressed a moment ago, that the brigade was not in that locality at all, and on several occasions, you've been mentioning the situation that reactions of this kind occurred where the brigade was, and that is based on faulty facts. It is just not true. What you are saying is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: There have been many testimonies about that. But let me ask you one more question now: You were the deputy commander and then commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade in 1993, and that is the year that the Court is interested in. Tell the Trial Chamber now, please, whether, on any occasion, a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade committed a war crime or crime against humanity, any single crime, "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We have concluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Mr. Nobilo. I turn to my colleagues. Judge Shahabuddeen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Colonel, I would like to take you back to the village of Ovnak. You said that the HVO units withdrew the people. How did you know that? Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: In relation to the reports by the police who were in the zone to secure the facilities there, on the basis of the reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Where were you when you received these reports? Where were you in relation to the village?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: Between the village of Ovnak and Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: How far away were you from the village?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: It's approximately three kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Whose police were they?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: It was security for the village, that is to say, the police units engaged on this assignment: The commander of the corps and the MUP police, that is to say, the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The police were on your side?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: In that zone, the police had the task of preventing any kind of destruction, such as burning houses, pilferage, or anything else that jeopardises the area, and that was its assignment. So the police was the military police. We had the civilian police and the military police, and they had a common assignment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: They were the military police of the Armija?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: The military police and the civilian police. The military police could act with members of the army if there were any problems, and the civilian police had competencies over the civilian portion and ensured communication from Zenica to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Did you discover why the people of Ovnak left the village with the HVO units?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I did not discover why, but I heard information about that, that they were told by the HVO units to do so. At that time, the people that were there in the monastery, they did not withdraw, and I ensured security for the monastery by using a unit, and then the representatives of UNPROFOR turned up, and they established the facts. I then transferred those people to a safe zone and returned them back to the monastery the next day. The representatives of the Red Cross and UNPROFOR were there in that zone. They were located there too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Did you find out why the HVO units advised the people to leave Ovnak?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Did your units drive out the people of Ovnak?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I have already stressed that I don't know for what reason, but the HVO units, together with the people, left. Now, for what reason they exerted this pressure, I don't know, and as I said a moment ago, for example, they did the same in another area, in the Kraljeva Sutjeska zone. Quite simply, without any reason, they left the zone, and that is what happened at Ovnak too because Ovnak was secured by the military and civilian police, and nobody could approach there apart from the people who were located there. So they ensured security both for the people and for the buildings and the monastery and everything else. I did not see any reason why the people, together with the HVO units, left, but I assess that there was probably some reason. Perhaps the HVO units exerted pressure on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Why did part of the population of Kakanj leave Kakanj? Did you find out?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I did not find that out either. For unknown reasons, just as with the Ovnak case, without any reason, they had the people withdraw. And in Kraljeva Sutjeska, there was no fighting, and the people left anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Were there other places from which the Croat population withdrew?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: There were. So apart from Ovnak, Kraljeva Sutjeska -- in Kraljeva Sutjeska, there is a very famous monastery, an even larger one, and some people remained there. The friars from the monastery stayed there, in that part, but there was no fighting there, and the people left without reason. And the case was similar in Vares.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: How long after the people left Ovnak did your units enter Ovnak?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: It was on the 9th of June at Ovnak. So that same day, that same day, during those events, the village was emptied. And I spent some time there, perhaps another day, because I had another assignment, and then I withdrew the unit from that zone. So the unit was withdrawn from that zone in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: What I'm trying to ask you to focus on is this: The people of Ovnak left and then, according to you, your units entered the village. What was the time span between the time when the people left Ovnak and the time when your units entered Ovnak?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: According to my assessment, from the morning until the afternoon. The people, together with the HVO units, left the village -- (Trial Chamber confers)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [to Judge Shahabuddeen] Yes? Could you hear the English translation? Can you hear the English interpretation? Can you hear the English interpretation, Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear the interpretation. Thank you very much. I am reading your answer on the screen before me. According to what I read, you said: "According to my assessment, from the morning until the afternoon. The people, together with the HVO units, left the village --" I'm still a little unclear about the answer to my question. What was the interval of time between when the people left Ovnak and when your units entered the village?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: From the morning until the afternoon. They left with the HVO units from the village. In the afternoon, we were able, that is to say, I got a report that there was no movement around the village. I got that report in the afternoon. And that led us to conclude that the village was probably empty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: And then the civilian police ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Rodrigues? Thank you, Judge Shahabuddeen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Colonel, I understood that the 7th Brigade began to be organised sometime in December 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: That is correct. The end of November 1992, that is when the corps command issued an order, the date was the 19th of November, I have the order here; that is to say, the establishment started at the end of November and then continued in December and January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: So you participated in the initial organisation of the brigade, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: At the end of December, I joined the brigade, and I was assistant chief of staff for operations and teaching, and that is the role I played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Is it possible to associate certain villages with the creation of the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: Is it possible to associate a few villages? I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Let me repeat the question. Is it possible to associate, to the formation of the 7th Brigade, any particular village? I am not trying to lead the question, but let me be more direct. The village of Nemila, does it mean anything to you in the context of the formation of the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: At the time when I came, no. Nemila is a small place near Zenica, and when the brigade was being established, the command was being established in Zenica, the 2nd Battalion in Zenica, the staff units in Zenica, the 1st Battalion in Travnik, and the 3rd Battalion in Kakanj. That is where the headquarters of the battalion was. And Nemila is a village that belongs to Zenica; that is to say, that there is a possibility that there were men in the brigade from that village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes, but this 7th Brigade, before becoming the 7th Muslim Brigade, was it not called the Nemila Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: When I came, that is to say, the end of December, the formation of the brigade had already started. And which units existed in Zenica earlier on and joined the 7th, that I really don't know, but I have been able to follow events from the formation in December onwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes. And the relationship between the 7th Brigade and the MOS ...

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: When the corps was established also in November, the 3rd Corps, all the units that were in the zone of the 3rd Corps grew into something else; that is to say, there were other units that grew into a brigade. Among others, there were units in many towns, Zenica included, that had different names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: So after the formation of the 7th Brigade, did it always retain the same structure or was that structure changed?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: The brigade was formed -- I didn't understand you. What are you referring to? The organisational structure of the unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I do not wish to suggest an answer. Wasn't a party of that brigade directly subordinated to the supreme headquarters?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: No, never. No, never. That is to say, that the brigade was always within the 3rd Corps and it always received orders from the 3rd Corps. Not a single part of the brigade was ever outside the brigade. All units that were within the brigade were within the system of command and control. The same system prevailed from the brigade towards the command of the corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Another question: Do you know the date when the events in Dusina occurred?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: What events are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: We have already spoken many times here, both the Defence and the President have referred to these events, certain acts that were committed in Dusina. Do you know the dates of those events?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: In relation to the crime in Dusina, I don't know about that, but I'm going to tell you about the elements that I am aware of. At that time, until January, the relations between the HVO units and the army were good. In January, I can't remember the exact date, HVO units forcefully entered the village of Merdani. On that occasion, the village of Merdani fell, and they expelled the population. The village of Merdani has a Bosniak population. On that occasion, they took two girls prisoner, I don't have their names and surnames here, but we do have the names and surnames of these girls --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting you, Colonel, but my question still is whether you know the date or not. You're talking about events. You're saying "in that period." You even indicated, in answer to a question, that on such and such a date, you were in office, but apparently you didn't know the exact date. You said that at that time you were in office, but you didn't know the date.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I was chief of staff. The village of Merdani that I'm talking about is a village next to Dusina, so please allow me to finish what I started. After this event in the village of Merdani, I received an order to take a company out of my 2nd Battalion and to attach them to the municipal staff in Zenica, and that is what I did, so it is in that zone that there was a company of mine. After the village of Merdani, I got a report saying that HVO units had attacked the direction of the TO staff in Zenica, and in that conflict, two of my men were killed and six were wounded, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Colonel, I apologise for interrupting, but what has that got to do with Dusina and the crimes committed in Dusina?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: I don't know about the crimes committed in Dusina. I'm telling you about the task --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: You don't even know the date --

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: -- when that crime was committed? You don't know the date? You knew that in that period, you were in office.

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: At that time, I was chief of staff. I don't know that a crime was committed in Dusina. I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting once more, and then I will finish, but I have difficulty in understanding the following: You don't know the date of the crimes of Dusina, but you say that at the time, you held such and such a position. I don't understand. How is it possible to be in office and yet not know the date?

utterances.speaker: AMIR KUBURA
utterances.text: That zone is a zone that was held by the municipal staff, that is to say, those units were in that zone. I was not in that zone. It was my company only that was there, and I got a report that my company was in the direction of this attack and that I had two of my men wounded, and six of my men -- two men were killed and six were wounded. I didn't hear anything about any other crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. I have no other questions.
